transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Lately I just don’t care about the art shows, the mentoring, or even my photography anymore. Nothing really feels worth doing, and I just can't bring myself to care about any of it.
Can you tell me, have you lost interest in these activities recently, or has this been a long-standing feeling for you?

This is a relatively recent change for me, not a lifelong feeling, though it has been hanging over me for most of the past year. It really set in after a very high-energy phase right after I retired fizzled out. Now, things I used to love like my photography or mentoring just feel like chores I can't bring myself to start.
Can you estimate more precisely when this feeling of not caring about your usual activities started, and did it begin gradually or quite suddenly after your high-energy phase ended?

It started about nine or ten months ago, not long after that high-energy overdrive period fizzled out. The change was actually quite sudden—I abruptly shifted from being constantly busy to just feeling completely listless. It has been hanging over me like a heavy cloud for most of this past year.

You mentioned this feeling of not caring started about nine or ten months ago, can you tell me if there was a specific event or period that triggered this change, or if it seemed to come out of the blue after your retirement?

It didn't happen right after I retired, nor did it come completely out of the blue. It actually followed a period of intense, chaotic over-activity where I took on far too many projects and commitments. Once that high-energy overdrive phase fizzled out, I suddenly collapsed into this heavy, listless state where I stopped caring about everything.
Have you experienced any periods of improved mood or increased energy since this listless state began, or has it been a persistent feeling over the past nine to ten months?

No, I haven't had any periods of improved mood or high energy since this crash began. That intense energy was entirely before this low phase, and for the past nine or ten months, it has just been a persistent, heavy, and joyless feeling.

Can you tell me if you have had any other episodes like this in your life before, or if this is the first time you've experienced such a prolonged period of feeling listless and uncaring about activities you once enjoyed?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. These severe swings and this prolonged listlessness are entirely new to me, and only began after my retirement.

You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but can you tell me if you've had any other periods in your life where you felt extremely high in energy and activity, similar to the overdrive phase before this listless period began?

No, I don't recall ever having any other periods of extreme high energy or overdrive prior to my retirement. That phase right after I left my job was really the first time it felt so intense and disruptive.

Given that you've experienced a significant change in mood and energy after retirement, and considering this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if you believe this current state is a response to the retirement itself or something unrelated?

I absolutely believe retirement played a major role, as leaving my structured career left me struggling with a total lack of boundaries. I tried to fill that void by overcommitting to far too many projects, which threw me into that chaotic overdrive and eventually led to this crash. It really feels like a direct, overwhelming reaction to failing to manage such a major life transition.

You've had this persistent low mood for about nine to ten months without any significant improvement, but can you tell me if you're experiencing any symptoms like significant changes in appetite, sleep patterns, or fatigue that have been consistent throughout this period?

My sleep has been terrible; I lie awake until two or three in the morning with my mind spinning, only to wake up before dawn feeling completely wrung out. I also feel incredibly slowed down and exhausted, as if I'm trying to wade through mud, though my appetite hasn't really been an issue.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of guilt or worthlessness about yourself or your situation during this time?

I feel like a complete and useless fraud, especially after having so many advantages in life. I keep replaying past mistakes from my career and marriage as if they're unforgivable sins, and since I let everyone down by dropping the ball on the exhibition and mentoring, I often think everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.

Can you tell me more about when these feelings of guilt and worthlessness started, and if they have been constant since the onset of your listless state, or have they varied in intensity over the past nine to ten months?

These feelings of being a useless old fraud started pretty much right after that high-energy phase fizzled out and this low period set in. They have been very constant and heavy, as I constantly replay past missteps and feel guilty about dropping the ball on my commitments.

Have you noticed any decrease in your ability to experience pleasure from activities that you once found enjoyable, such as your photography, or has the lack of interest been the primary issue for you?

It is definitely both a complete lack of interest and a total loss of pleasure. Activities like photography and mentoring, which used to bring me immense joy and really light me up, now just feel like chores I can't even be bothered to start. Nothing feels worth doing anymore, and there is absolutely no joy left in any of it.

You mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but considering the duration of about nine to ten months, can you tell me if you're concerned that this might be a recurring issue for you in the future, or do you feel this is a one-time response to your retirement and life changes?

To be honest, I'm really not sure what the future holds or if this is something that will happen again. Right now, I'm just so overwhelmed by how difficult this retirement transition has been and how heavy my low mood is that I haven't been able to think that far ahead. I'm just trying to figure out how to get through each day as it comes.

You've had this episode for about nine to ten months without significant improvement, but can you tell me if you've had any shorter periods of feeling somewhat better or more hopeful during this time, even if they were brief?
No, I haven't really experienced any of those brief periods of feeling better or more hopeful. It has just felt like one continuous, heavy cloud ever since the crash started.

Given that you've experienced a single episode of depression so far, do you think the fact that it started after a significant life event like retirement and has lasted for about nine to ten months might suggest that it could be a one-time adjustment issue, or are you concerned it might indicate a more recurrent condition?

While it did start after retirement, it hasn't been a simple, continuous low. This heavy, joyless phase was actually preceded by that intense, high-energy overdrive where I felt on top of the world and quite irritable. These dramatic swings between extreme highs and deep lows make me worry that it's more than just a one-time adjustment issue.
Can you describe in more detail the irritability you experienced during the high-energy overdrive phase, and how it compared to your usual behavior and mood before retirement?

During those high-energy weeks, I felt absolutely "high on life," but I became incredibly snappish and would get downright furious with my wife if she so much as suggested I slow down or reschedule anything. In my past career as a corporate strategist, I was always a very driven person, but I had never experienced those intense, irrational flashes of anger over such simple suggestions.

Can you clarify if the intense irritability and anger you experienced during the high-energy phase were part of a broader pattern of mood instability, or were they isolated incidents triggered by specific situations or stressors?

They weren't isolated incidents; they were part of a broader, weeks-long phase where I felt completely "high on life" and was constantly on the go. During that overdrive period, I would get highly defensive, snappish, and downright furious—especially with my wife—if anyone tried to suggest I slow down or reschedule my overlapping projects.
Have you experienced any other episodes of intense irritability or mood swings similar to the ones you had during the high-energy overdrive phase, either before or after this current low period?

No, I have never experienced other episodes like this before. These intense mood swings—both the high-energy overdrive and this current crash—only started a few months after I retired. While I was always a driven person during my career, I never had these kinds of extreme, disruptive highs or irritable periods before this recent cycle.

Considering your experience of both a high-energy overdrive phase followed by a deep low, do you think it's possible that you might be experiencing a condition that involves more than just depression, given the significant mood swings you've described?

I think you’re right, and my primary care provider actually noticed those extreme swings as well, which is why he referred me here for a possible mood disorder. Looking back, the stark contrast between that chaotic, high-energy overdrive and this dark, listless low really does feel like much more than just standard depression.

Can you tell me if you have experienced any other episodes of extreme mood swings, similar to the high-energy overdrive phase followed by a deep low, at any other point in your life before retirement?
No, I don't recall experiencing mood swings like this at any other point in my life before retirement. This pattern of extreme highs and deep lows really seemed to start only after I retired.

Can you clarify if the pattern of extreme highs followed by deep lows is something you're concerned will continue, or do you believe it was a singular response to the stress of retirement and adjusting to a new life phase?

I'm really not sure what to think anymore because I am feeling so incredibly low right now. I haven't really thought about whether this will be a permanent pattern or if it was just a reaction to my retirement. At this point, I'm just trying to make it through each day.

Considering your experience of both high-energy overdrive and deep low phases, do you think the fact that you had a distinct high phase before this low phase might indicate a more specific type of mood disorder, such as bipolar disorder, rather than just a depressive episode?

Yes, that is actually the term my primary care physician mentioned when he referred me to psychiatry. It is a bit daunting to wrap my head around, but given how extreme the contrast was between that intense overdrive and this current dark period, it certainly seems to fit. I'm just hoping to get some clarity and figure out how to get some relief.

Can you tell me more about how you felt during the high-energy overdrive phase, specifically if you experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, which might help differentiate between a bipolar disorder and a major depressive episode?

I didn't have any hallucinations like hearing or seeing things, though I was buzzing with energy, talking constantly, and my mind was racing. However, I did have an incredibly inflated sense of my own capabilities, genuinely believing I was the only person who could save these start-ups and write the definitive strategy book. Looking back, it was an extreme overconfidence that felt almost unrealistic, but I didn't experience any other kinds of delusions.

During your high-energy overdrive phase, did you ever feel like your thoughts were being controlled by an external force, or did you have any delusions of grandeur beyond just feeling overconfident in your abilities?

No, I never felt like any external force was controlling my thoughts. However, my confidence went far beyond normal overconfidence—I genuinely believed I was the only person on the planet who could save those start-ups, fix the arts council, and write the definitive strategy book, as if I possessed a unique, special insight.
During your high-energy overdrive phase, did you experience any symptoms where you felt like you had special powers, were on a mission, or had a special connection to something or someone?

Yes, during that high-energy phase, I really did feel like I was uniquely gifted and almost on a mission. I felt like I was the only person capable of saving those start-ups, organizing the arts council, and writing the definitive book on corporate strategy. It truly felt as though I possessed a special level of insight that no one else on the planet had.
Can you estimate how long the high-energy overdrive phase lasted before you crashed into this low period, and did you require less sleep than usual during that time?

That high-energy overdrive phase seemed to last for several months before I suddenly crashed into this low period. As for my sleep during that time, I honestly can't quite remember or be sure about what my sleep patterns were like back then.

Can you tell me if, during your high-energy overdrive phase, you experienced a decreased need for sleep, such as feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep, and did this occur nearly every day during that period?
I honestly don't recall if I needed less sleep or felt rested on fewer hours back then. Everything was such a blur during those busy months that I just can't remember what my sleep was like.
Did you experience any periods of abnormally elevated or irritable mood during the high-energy overdrive phase that lasted for at least four consecutive days?

Yes, absolutely. That high-energy phase lasted for weeks, which is well over four days, and during that entire time I felt incredibly "high on life." I was also extremely irritable and snappish, getting downright furious if my wife suggested I slow down or reschedule anything.
During your high-energy overdrive phase, did you engage in any excessive or reckless behaviors, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or impulsive decisions?

I didn't really engage in reckless behaviors like excessive spending or dangerous driving during that time. However, I did make a lot of impulsive, overambitious commitments to projects and trips that I couldn't possibly keep. It was more about overcommitting myself to everything than doing anything dangerous.

Can you confirm if the high-energy overdrive phase occurred only once before this current low period, or have you had similar episodes of extremely high energy and mood elevation at any other point in your life?

I can only clearly recall this recent high-energy period that happened after my retirement. I don't recall having any other extreme episodes of high energy or mood elevation like that earlier in my life.
